visualInspection.observed: A near courtyard, brick facade, stairs, props and playable ground dominate the frame. The two native images are byte-identical and no new visible gap or surface disruption is seen.
visualInspection.ashCoverage: Limited or unestablished from this view alone. The prominent near ground and structures are not all the changed backdrop mesh. Equality here is not strong evidence of backdrop-ground quality by itself.

visualInspection.observed: The foreground tiled roof, rooftop equipment and building silhouettes match exactly. The images contain no new visible roof/skyline discontinuity attributable to the ground change.
visualInspection.ashCoverage: The main visible surface is roof geometry. Possible distant ground glimpses are too limited to treat this byte-identical pair as comprehensive ash coverage.

visualInspection.observed: Exposed terrain beyond the city boundary is visible around and between the brick/corrugated blocks. The broad surface, texture layout and building-ground contact remain visually continuous. No new large hole or long seam is recognized.
visualInspection.ashCoverage: The affected visible terrain is the boundary-exterior ground and the surface bands where actual old/new pixels differ. Do not label the entire lower half as backdrop ash: nearer ordinary ground and the white marking are mixed into that image region.

Other changed pixels have maximum channel difference18. This is a real deterministic raster difference, but the native-sized pair does not establish a material visual quality loss from it.

conclusions.supported: The723456→1256 ash-triangle change shows no demonstrated material visual regression in these4 controlled low-tier720x405 stills. The city_edge and horizon_ground pairs provide the meaningful visible ground coverage; street and roof provide weaker backdrop-specific coverage.

A claim that every lower-frame or left-edge surface belongs to the ash mesh.
Visual preservation at medium/high quality, higher backing resolutions or while the camera moves.

conclusions.mechanismHypothesis: Changing subdivision can alter interpolation/rasterization and depth ordering at overlapping coplanar-patch or ground-marking edges. This is plausible from the source and localization of differences, but this review does not measure the specific GPU mechanism.
conclusions.nextConcreteValidation: Before applying this visual judgement to the initially selected medium tier, lock and record the intended tier for the same visible-ground pairs, capture its actual native pixels with stable repeats, and inspect the marking edge and overlap bands. Moving-view behavior remains a separate unmeasured scope.
